title: Garden and Thorn Revisited
premise: Silas Reyes, last apprentice of the Thornwright Guild, has survived five years of the magic ban by selling charms too small to notice—until a mute child arrives speaking the Old Tongue, the language that binds kings. The child is a living key, and the thing wearing King Aldric's crown is a hollow god the guild helped imprison centuries ago, now working itself free. Silas must gather the scattered remnants of his dead guild's knowledge while evading the Crown's witch-hunters and confronting the truth that his masters didn't die out—they were purged for creating the binding in the first place. In the end, Silas realizes the only way to unbind the king is to take the binding into himself: he becomes the new vessel, trading his freedom and name for the kingdom's survival, while the child—revealed as the guild's reborn memory—carries his story forward.
about_author: O. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about institutions that outlive their sins, and live quietly with two cats and an unlicensed garden.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Knocked at Dusk
chapters.summary: Silas Reyes, POV. Silas sells a luck-charm to a baker, hides his guild tattoo from a patrol, and returns to his shuttered shop to find a child waiting on his step, speaking words that make his wards scream. The emotional beat is dread wrapped in longing—the first time in five years anyone has needed him for what he truly is.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Deciphering the child's speech, Silas finds his master's hidden ledger: the Thornwrights didn't fade—they bound something into the royal line, and the binding is failing. Beat: guilt curdling into resolve as Silas understands his survival was engineered, not accidental.

chapters.title: A Court of Ash and Etiquette
chapters.summary: Silas infiltrates the palace as a charm-seller to the nobility, glimpsing King Aldric—and the wrongness behind his eyes. POV shifts briefly to Vessa Corrane, the witch-hunter captain who suspects him. Beat: vertigo of proximity; power up close is more horrifying than rumor.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Kindness
chapters.summary: Vessa, POV. Vessa interrogates Silas but lets him go, revealing she hunts magic because it took her sister—not out of loyalty. She warns him away from the palace. Beat: uneasy kinship between two people on opposite sides of the same wound.

chapters.title: Salt in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Following ledger clues to a drowned guildhouse beneath the harbor, Silas recovers the binding rite and learns its cost: a living vessel. The child begins remembering things no child should know. Beat: awe giving way to horror as the price becomes clear.

chapters.title: The King Who Screamed Politely
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. At a royal audience, Aldric privately begs Silas for death in perfect Old Tongue before the crown-thing reasserts control. Silas escapes by the skin of his teeth. Beat: compassion weaponized—the enemy is also a prisoner, complicating every easy choice.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Green Wax
chapters.summary: Vessa, POV. Vessa discovers her own superiors have been feeding citizens to the crown-thing to delay the unbinding, buying stability with lives. She burns her orders and goes to Silas. Beat: disillusionment—the institution she served was the monster's accomplice.

chapters.title: Night of the Unraveling
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The binding fails early; the crown-thing floods the capital with compulsion, and the city turns on itself hunting the child. Silas, Vessa, and the child fight through burning streets toward the throne room. Beat: desperate momentum, everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Garden and Thorn
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Climax: in the throne room, Silas attempts the rite but cannot complete it without a willing vessel—and Aldric, briefly himself, chooses to hold the thing still long enough. The child speaks the final word through Silas, tearing the god loose. Beat: sacrifice refracted—no one escapes clean.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Remembers
chapters.summary: Silas, then the child, POV. The god, unbound, cannot survive outside a vessel; Silas takes it into himself, his name dissolving even as the city wakes free. Months later, the child—now the guild reborn—tends a quiet garden over the sealed vault where Silas sleeps, dreaming. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity surrendered, story preserved.
